title: Task 2 — Free university education
prompt:
Some people believe that university education should be free for everyone, while others argue that students should pay at least part of the cost. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

Write at least 250 words.
checklist: A clear position stated in the introduction
Both views discussed with reasons or examples
Two developed body paragraphs, not a list
A conclusion that restates your position
modelAnswer:
Whether university should be free is a question of priorities as much as money. While free education widens access, asking graduates to contribute is fairer to taxpayers and can protect quality. In my view, a mixed model works best.

Supporters of free university argue that tuition fees discourage talented students from low-income families. When entry depends on ability rather than background, society benefits from a larger pool of skilled graduates. Countries that abolished fees have seen participation rise, particularly among first-generation students.

On the other hand, university education creates substantial private benefits. Graduates typically earn more over a lifetime, so asking them to repay part of the cost after they start working is reasonable. This model also protects public budgets, which must fund schools and healthcare as well.

The strongest solution combines both principles: low or no upfront fees, funded by income-contingent repayment once a graduate earns above a threshold. This removes the barrier at entry while keeping the system sustainable. Free education sounds generous, but a fair repayment system delivers the same access more reliably.
